RSA.costNote: Public key size increases from 256 bytes to 1,952 bytes

alternatives.rationale: Primary NIST standardized digital signature algorithm at security level 3
Hybrid composite signature for backward compatibility with legacy verifiers
Stateless hash-based signature; ideal for firmware, root CAs, and audit logs requiring zero lattice assumptions

ECDSA.costNote: Public key size expands from 64 bytes to 1,312 bytes

alternatives.rationale: NIST security level 2 signature standard matching classical 128-bit security
Dual-signature composite for zero-risk phased enterprise rollout
Compact signatures for bandwidth-constrained environments (requires constant-time floating-point arithmetic)

Diffie-Hellman.latencyNote: +1 TLS handshake roundtrip (1.2ms added network latency)
Diffie-Hellman.costNote: Requires client-side TLS 1.3 hybrid KEM extension support

alternatives.rationale: Recommended by NIST, NSA CNSA 2.0, and IETF for all TLS 1.3 connections
Level 5 parameter for classified and ultra-long-lived national security secrets
Gold standard hybrid KEM adopted in OpenSSL 3.4 and modern browsers

DSA.latencyNote: Significantly improves verification throughput over legacy DSA
DSA.costNote: Immediate deprecation required; update verification keyrings

alternatives.rationale: Replaces legacy DSA with state-of-the-art lattice signatures

Ed25519.costNote: Replace SSH host keys and API authorization keys

alternatives.rationale: High-performance lattice signatures for SSH and authentication microservices

X25519.costNote: Minimal compute penalty; widely standardized in IETF

alternatives.rationale: IETF post-quantum standard draft adopted by Cloudflare, Google, and Apple

MD5.costNote: Drop-in code replacement for digest and checksum routines

alternatives.rationale: Standard cryptographic replacement for broken legacy digests

SHA-1.latencyNote: Native CPU SHA extensions match SHA-1 throughput
SHA-1.costNote: Zero payload increase for standard 256-bit hash outputs

alternatives.rationale: Provides 192-bit quantum margin; complies with CNSA 2.0

DES.latencyNote: AES-NI provides up to 5x faster hardware encryption than software DES
DES.costNote: Migrate database column sizes and key stores to 256-bit

alternatives.rationale: Authenticated encryption with 128-bit quantum security margin

3DES.latencyNote: Significantly faster execution due to hardware AES-NI instructions

alternatives.rationale: Eliminates Sweet32 collision attacks and provides robust Grover resistance
High-speed constant-time stream cipher resistant to quantum attacks

AES-128.latencyNote: Virtually indistinguishable performance on modern CPUs with AES-NI
AES-128.costNote: Bump key generation parameter from 16 to 32 bytes

alternatives.rationale: Mitigates Grover's quadratic search reduction (maintains 128-bit security)

TLS 1.0.costNote: Drops outdated legacy client browsers unable to negotiate modern TLS

alternatives.rationale: Modern secure transport with forward secrecy immune to harvest-now-decrypt-later
